title: "How many packages you can use"
knitr:
  opts_chunk:

---

```{r}
#| include: false
# The numbers come from data-raw/package-availability.R
a <- jsonlite::read_json("package-availability.json")
cran <- a$cran
share <- cran$shares
bioc <- a$bioconductor
num <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")
or_list <- function(x) paste0(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), " or ", tail(x, 1))
date <- as.Date(a$date)
most <- if (share$usable > 0.5 && bioc$on_bioconda_share > 0.5) "most" else "much"
```

For years, the answer to "can I use conda for R?" was "only if your packages happen to be on conda-forge". That's no longer the case: with conda-forge, bioconda, and packages built from source, `r most` of CRAN and Bioconductor is usable in a Pixi project. This article has the numbers, for deciding whether Pixi is ready for your R work.

The numbers are from `r as.integer(format(date, "%d"))` `r format(date, "%B %Y")`, with Pixi `r a$pixi`. They'll change as conda-forge, bioconda and Pixi do.

## CRAN

Of CRAN's `r num(cran$packages)` packages:

| | Packages | Share |
|---|---|---|
| On conda-forge | `r num(cran$conda_forge)` | `r pct(share$conda_forge)` |
| Built from source by rpix | `r num(cran$source)` | `r pct(share$source)` |
| **Usable through Pixi and rpix** | **`r num(cran$usable)`** | **`r pct(share$usable)`** |
| Not yet: a dependency isn't on conda-forge | `r num(cran$blocked_dependency)` | `r pct(share$blocked_dependency)` |
| Not yet: needs a system library R doesn't bring | `r num(cran$blocked_system)` | `r pct(share$blocked_system)` |

conda-forge has fewer packages than CRAN, but the ones that matter most: `r num(cran$top_on_conda_forge)` of the `r num(cran$top)` packages other CRAN packages depend on most, and `r pct(cran$conda_forge_current)` of its R packages are at CRAN's current version.

**Built from source** is what `pixi_add()` offers for a CRAN package that isn't on conda-forge: Pixi builds it from CRAN's source, with its dependencies from conda-forge (see [Finding packages](finding-packages.html)). A package counts when all its dependencies (`Depends`, `Imports` and `LinkingTo`) are on conda-forge or come with R, and its `SystemRequirements` need nothing beyond what conda-forge's R brings (such as curl, cairo, libxml2 or GSL) and the build tools rpix adds (Rust, CMake, pkg-config, Java). Building one takes a minute or two. A random sample of 25 of them all built and loaded, on macOS.

### What's still missing

`r if (cran$blocked_dependency > cran$blocked_system) "Most" else "Some"` of the packages that don't work yet depend on a package that isn't on conda-forge either. For `r num(cran$chains_blocked)` of these `r num(cran$blocked_dependency)`, that dependency can be built from source too, so once Pixi can build packages that depend on other packages built from source ([prefix-dev/pixi#6925](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi/issues/6925)), rpix can build the whole chain. `r if (cran$rest_bioc_or_library > cran$rest / 2) "Most" else "Some"` of the rest need a Bioconductor package (often `r or_list(cran$bioc_dependencies)`), which needs [prefix-dev/pixi#6994](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi/issues/6994), or a system library such as GDAL or libsndfile.

| | Usable | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Today | `r num(cran$usable)` | `r pct(share$usable)` |
| Building missing dependencies from source too | `r num(cran$usable_chains)` | `r pct(share$usable_chains)` |
| And Bioconductor dependencies from bioconda | `r num(cran$usable_bioconda)` | `r pct(share$usable_bioconda)` |

## Bioconductor

bioconda has `r if (bioc$on_bioconda_share >= 0.95) "essentially all" else if (bioc$on_bioconda_share > 0.5) "most" else "some"` of Bioconductor `r bioc$bioconda_release`, for R `r bioc$bioconda_r`: `r num(bioc$on_bioconda)` of its `r num(bioc$bioconda_release_software)` software packages, `r pct(bioc$at_version_share)` of them at their `r bioc$bioconda_release` version or newer. Add them with a `bioc::` prefix, or without one: `pixi_add()` looks on bioconda when a package isn't on conda-forge.

Some things to know:

- **Use R `r bioc$bioconda_r`.** `r if (bioc$release != bioc$bioconda_release) paste0("Bioconductor ", bioc$release, ", for R ", bioc$release_r, ", isn't on bioconda yet. That waits on conda-forge building its R packages for R ", bioc$release_r, ", which only a few are so far.") else paste0("bioconda has Bioconductor ", bioc$release, " for R ", bioc$bioconda_r, ".")`
- **Annotation and data packages**, such as org.Hs.eg.db, download their data with an install script, which Pixi only runs in projects that allow it. `pixi_add()` offers to allow it.
- **Windows:** bioconda doesn't build its packages for Windows. Bioconductor packages that don't depend on other Bioconductor packages do build from source there, from [Bioconductor's git mirror on GitHub](https://github.com/bioc), but rpix doesn't offer that yet.

## Platforms

The source builds were measured on macOS. Packages of each kind (pure R, R's recommended packages, C, C++, Fortran, Rust and Bioconductor) also build on Linux, and on Windows with what rpix adds for building there.

## How these were counted

- **CRAN:** every package in CRAN's package database, with its dependencies and `SystemRequirements`.
- **conda-forge and bioconda:** the packages in their channel data, for `r a$platform`, matched by name (`r-<name>` and `bioconductor-<name>`).
- **System requirements:** read with Posit's [r-system-requirements](https://github.com/rstudio/r-system-requirements) rules. A language standard ("C++17"), make, and tools only needed when the package runs (pandoc, Python) count as needing nothing.

The script that counts them is [`data-raw/package-availability.R`](https://github.com/roaldarbol/rpix/blob/main/data-raw/package-availability.R).
